# Resurgamus Horizon

> Lightweight open-source self-hosted secrets manager and vault for automation,
> CI/CD and AI/MCP agents. Horizon encrypts secrets at rest, issues scoped and
> auditable credentials, and runs single-node or highly available.

Also described as: secrets manager, secrets management, self-hosted vault,
AI vault, MCP vault.

What it is:

- AGPL-3.0-or-later, with a commercial license available
- complete public feature set, no Enterprise feature gates
- no SaaS dependency, no telemetry, no lock-in
- lightweight: one API container plus PostgreSQL, no external coordinator
- native MCP server and MCP Hub, so an agent can use a credential it may
  never read
- scoped, auditable, revocable credentials
- dynamic secrets (PostgreSQL, MySQL, LDAP) and a built-in PKI engine
- quantum-resistant posture: X25519MLKEM768 TLS key exchange (FIPS 203) and
  optional ML-DSA-65 certificates (FIPS 204)
- single-node and high-availability deployments
- Docker, Podman, Kubernetes, Linux, macOS and BSD (FreeBSD, OpenBSD, NetBSD);
  see the compatibility matrix for what is tested on each
- SLSA Build L1 provenance, Cosign signatures and CycloneDX SBOM

Canonical public source: https://github.com/JR-Shdw/Horizon
License: AGPL-3.0-or-later
